title: On-call & Incident Response: Communications, Templates, and Runbooks
author: Alicia Chen
content:
Overview

This document consolidates our incident response process, on-call rotation guidance, runbook structure, postmortem templates, game day plans, and ready-to-use status page and customer communications. It is intended for on-call engineers, incident commanders (ICs), product and customer success reps who will be involved in customer-facing updates.

Goals
- Reduce time-to-detect and time-to-restore for production incidents.
- Provide clear, repeatable processes for incident handling and communication.
- Preserve high-quality postmortems to drive continuous improvement.

Scope
Covers incidents affecting Redwood-hosted systems and public customer-facing APIs (Hosted API, Console, Dedicated control plane). For private/on-prem incidents, follow customer-specific runbooks in eng-private-deployments/reference-architectures.

Incident process (high-level)
1. Detection & Triage
   - Alerting systems (PagerDuty, Prometheus AlertManager, CloudWatch alarms) surface symptoms.
   - PagerDuty escalation policy: first on-call (SRE) for 10 minutes, then senior on-call for 10 minutes, then on-call manager.
2. Mobilize
   - Acknowledge on PagerDuty, join the incident channel (#inc-{incident-id}).
   - IC is appointed (first responder becomes IC unless escalated). IC responsibilities listed below.
3. Contain & Mitigate
   - Execute runbooks for known failure modes.
   - If unknown, collect diagnostics (logs, traces, recent deploys, config changes).
4. Communicate
   - Update internal channel every 15 minutes during P0/P1 incidents.
   - Publish status page (see templates) for customer-impacting incidents within 30 minutes.
5. Resolve & Recover
   - Remove mitigating controls only after verifying system stability.
6. Post-incident
   - Run postmortem within 3 business days; publish summary and corrective action plan.

Incident severity definitions
- P0 (Critical): System-wide outage or degraded service causing severe customer impact (SLO breach, >50% traffic errors). Response: immediate page, all-hands.
- P1 (High): Significant feature or cluster outage impacting a subset of customers or causing partial degradation.
- P2 (Medium): Localized issue; functional but degraded.
- P3 (Low): Minor impact, background task failures, or operational alerts without customer impact.

Runbook structure (standard template)
Each runbook should follow this headerless structure so responders can quickly scan:
- Title: short, imperative (e.g., "Restore model-controller cluster").
- Severity & scope: affected services and likely symptoms.
- PagerDuty signals: alert names and thresholds.
- Quick-fix checklist (3–6 bullets) for immediate mitigation.
- Diagnostics: commands and dashboards to check (CLI and links).
- Recovery steps (ordered, numbered).
- Rollback/rollback verification steps (if applicable).
- Post-incident notes: known root causes, links to related incidents, owners.

Example runbook snippet
1) Symptom: high 5xx on /v1/generate across ca-central.
2) Quick checks:
   - Check cluster health: kubectl -n runtime get pods -o wide | grep model-controller
   - Check recent deploys: git log --since="2 hours" --pretty=oneline origin/main
3) Immediate mitigation:
   - Scale down model-controller replicas to 0 and back to desired (kubectl scale deploy model-controller --replicas=0) to force warm restart.
4) If persists: failover traffic to us-east region (routing playbook link).

Ownership and escalation
- Incident Commander (IC): coordinates triage, assigns roles (scribe, triage, mitigation). Expected to be a senior on-call or the first on-call responder if they have runbook familiarity.
- Scribe: records timeline and decisions in the incident doc.
- Engineering lead: approves cross-team changes and customer messaging.
- Customer Success / PR: drafts external comms for customer-impact incidents.

On-call rotations and responsibilities
- Rotation model: 7-day primary on-call for SREs and engineers responsible for runtime services; 24/7 coverage via follow-the-sun escalation for major incidents.
- Handover checklist (to be posted in weekly rotation channel):
  - Confirm PagerDuty schedule is active and contact info correct.
  - Verify alert inbox & runbook access.
  - Note known issues and ongoing postmortems.
- Time allowance: Responders are expected to be available to respond to pages within their scheduled shift; primary on-call should not be assigned >20% of workweek to uninterrupted deep work.

Game days and training
- Frequency: Quarterly system-level game days and monthly service-level drills.
- Objectives: validate runbooks, test failover playbooks, practice IC/scribe roles, exercise customer comms.
- Post-game-day: publish lessons learned and required runbook updates within 5 business days.

Status page update templates
- Purpose: provide short, accurate updates to customers via status.redwood.ai. Use the templates below and post in #inc-{id}-comm when publishing.

Status page: initial (within 30m)
Title: Investigating – Degraded response from Redwood Hosted API (region specific)
Body: We are investigating reports of elevated error rates for text generation requests in {region}. Our engineers are actively investigating. Impact: requests may fail or return errors for some customers. Next update: within 15–30 minutes.

Status page: update (periodic)
Title: Update – Engineering investigating root cause
Body: Engineers have identified that recent autoscaling events are correlated with increased 5xx rates. We are performing mitigations (scaling controllers, failing over region traffic). Impact: partial customer impact persists. Next update: within 15 minutes or when impact changes.

Status page: resolved
Title: Resolved – Service restored for Redwood Hosted API (region)
Body: The issue causing elevated error rates has been mitigated and services are operating within normal parameters. Root cause analysis is in progress; we will publish a postmortem within 3 business days if this was P1/P0.

Customer communications (email/CS template)
- Use short subject lines and be transparent in the first sentence. Include impact, affected customers, mitigation steps, and ETA for next update. 

Template: initial customer email
Subject: Service impact: Elevated errors for Hosted API in {region}
Hi {CustomerName},
We are investigating elevated error rates for the Hosted API affecting {region}. Some requests may fail or return errors. Our engineering team is actively working on mitigations. We will send another update within 30 minutes. If you need immediate assistance or to escalate, reply to this message or open a support ticket at support.redwood.ai.

Template: follow-up customer email
Subject: Update: Mitigation in progress for Hosted API impact in {region}
Hi {CustomerName},
Update: We are performing targeted mitigations (scaling controllers, regional failover). Impact remains for a subset of requests. We do not currently expect data loss. We will send a final resolution update when service is restored.

Template: resolution & postmortem notice
Subject: Resolved: Hosted API incident in {region} – Postmortem forthcoming
Hi {CustomerName},
The issue affecting the Hosted API in {region} has been resolved. We are preparing a postmortem with root cause and corrective actions and will share it within 3 business days. If you saw any specific failures we should investigate, please reply with the request IDs or timestamps.

Postmortem template (to be completed within 3 business days for P0/P1)
- Title: Short, descriptive.
- Incident SEV: P0/P1/P2.
- Date/time window: detection -> resolved.
- Summary: executive 2–3 sentence summary.
- Impact: affected customers, services, and SLO impact.
- Timeline: ordered bullets with timestamps and actor (IC, SRE, Eng).
- Root cause: factual description.
- Contributing factors: environmental, deploys, monitoring gaps.
- Remediation & action items: owner and target completion date per item.
- Lessons learned: process, tool, or runbook changes.
- Public summary: 1–2 paragraph explanation suitable for customers.

Incident communications playbook (internal steps)
1) Immediately on page: create incident channel and incident document (use template).
2) IC assigns roles (scribe, triage lead, mitigation lead).
3) Scribe records timeline and every decision; preserve logs and link to dashboards.
4) Engineering lead reviews customer messages before publish.
5) CS rep drafts customer comms using templates and posts to #inc-{id}-comm for review.
6) After resolution: IC triggers postmortem ownership and schedule.

Scribing and documentation expectations
- Record every action and decision with timestamps.
- Keep the incident doc concise: do not log command output in full; link to logs or attach artifacts.
- Capture why decisions were made, not just what was done.

Retention and confidentiality
- Incident documents are internal by default and retained for 3 years. For customer-sensitive incidents, set confidentiality to "restricted" and follow Legal review process (security-and-compliance/risk-and-exceptions).

Appendix: quick CLI & dashboard checks
- kubectl -n runtime get pods -o wide | grep model-controller
- curl -sS https://status.redwood.ai/api/status | jq
- grafana dashboard links: runtime/latency-overview, api/error-rate
